rv.q: I saw the play just days after it opened Dec. 5 and it ranks as some of the best stage storytelling I’ve seen since prior to the pandemic.
The svelte nature of the scenes also serves the humor, of which there is plenty.
It’s one production that audiences won’t soon forget.
The Greenhouse production deserves to be seen both as a sensitive examination of one of the country’s major social problems and as a splendid piece of stagecraft.
What do we celebrate at this time of the year, if NOT the prospect of rebirth, restoration and a fresh path opening the way to peace?

This play undoubtedly will resonate strongly with anyone affected by alcoholism. At the same time, the production too often is content to simply skim the surface of addiction without providing meaningful further exploration.
This is 90 minutes ( no intermission) of sheer artistry in storytelling and although it is not typical holiday fare, is indeed a play that you should try to see.
Combined with a great script and well-paced, polished production, it seems destined to be a hit.

cn.t: Critics praise this straightforward addiction drama for balancing humor with unflinching realism about alcoholism. The play resonates as meaningful, well-paced theater that entertains while tackling its difficult subject without triviality.
